extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: TextVQA contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reasoning about text to answer. The dataset is designed to facilitate progress on Visual Question Answering models that can read and reason about text in images.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.publisher: Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were selected from Open Images v3 dataset from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). A three-stage pipeline was used for crowd-sourcing: (1) annotators identified images containing text, (2) 1-2 questions per image were collected requiring reading text to answer, (3) 10 answers were collected for each question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from Open Images v3 dataset. 100 random images from each category were sampled, OCR was run to compute average number of OCR boxes per category, and categories were weighted for sampling based on normalized OCR box counts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images without text were filtered out using forced-choice yes/no flags from annotators. Questions were filtered where majority of workers marked flags for: no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, or unanswerable. Hand-crafted questions with known answers were used to identify and filter out bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: OCR model (Rosetta) was run on images to extract word tokens. Images were filtered to 28,408 images containing text. Questions where majority of workers marked quality flags were removed. Bad annotators were filtered using hand-crafted validation questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Stage 1: Annotators identified images containing text using yes/no flag. Stage 2: Annotators provided 1-2 questions per image requiring reading text to answer, with instructions to ensure questions require reading text and second question has different answer from first. Stage 3: 10 answers were collected per question. Annotators were given four flag options: no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, unanswerable.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions. 3 or more annotators agree on most common answer for 97.9% of questions.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rosetta OCR system for text detection and recognition
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset addresses an important problem for visually impaired users. The VizWiz study found that up to 21% of questions from visually-impaired users involve reading and reasoning about text in images (e.g., 'what temperature is my oven set to?', 'what denomination is this bill?').
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The model often predicts 'new york' for city-related questions. For yes/no questions, 'yes' is the more common answer (4.71% of dataset). The most common answer 'yes' is majority answer for only 4.71% of dataset. Yes/no questions make up only 5.55% of dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: 8.9% of questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens, which the current model cannot handle. The model has strong dependency on OCR quality - if OCR misses text, predictions can be wrong. OCR fails at detecting rotated, unstructured (e.g., scribbles), or partially occluded text. The gap between human performance (85.01%) and machine performance (26.56%) is significantly larger than on VQA 2.0.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is split into train (34,602 questions), validation (5,000 questions), and test (5,734 questions) sets with no image overlap between sets. The dataset is designed to benchmark VQA models' ability to read and reason about text in images, complementary to VQA 2.0.
